audits.body:
Cloning https://aur.archlinux.org/printbar.git...
Cloned printbar
Analyzing printbar AUR package with openrouter/free
Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD contains a standard source definition pointing to the official GitHub archive (`https://github.com/mryll/printbar/archive/refs/tags/v0.5.2.tar.gz`). The source URL is legitimate and matches the package version. The associated SHA256 checksum is present and valid (not SKIPped). 

During `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare`, the build process is halted before any code execution—only the source is fetched and parsed. The `--nobuild` and `--noprepare` flags prevent any `prepare()`, `build()`, or `package()` steps from running, meaning no code from the source archive is executed. Extraction of the tarball writes files to disk but does not run them. Therefore, neither of the specified commands would execute malicious code. Standard VCS source definitions with proper checksums are normal and expected in AUR packages—they do not constitute a supply-chain risk in this context.
</details>
<evidence></evidence>
<summary>The source is a legitimate GitHub archive with a valid checksum, and the build flags prevent any code execution during the audit.</summary>

+ Initial PKGBUILD audit complete -- The source is a legitimate GitHub archive with a valid checksum, and the build flags prevent any code execution during the audit.

The sha256sums field provides a checksum for verification, which is standard practice and not indicative of tampering. Dependencies listed (cargo, gcc-libs, cups, libnotify, xdg-utils, ttf-jetbrains-mono-nerd) are typical for a Waybar printer monitor and do not involve suspicious network activity. No scripts or commands are present that download, execute, or modify system files beyond the normal packaging workflow (e.g., no curl|bash, no eval, no base64‑encoded blobs). The source is a static tarball from the official upstream tag, satisfying reproducibility requirements. Therefore, no evidence of malicious or dangerous behavior is found.
</details>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This is a standard PKGBUILD for a Rust application (`printbar`) that monitors printers for the Waybar status bar. The source is fetched from the package's own upstream GitHub repository at a pinned tag (`v0.5.2`), and a SHA-256 checksum is provided and correctly applied. The build process uses `cargo build --release --locked` with a stable Rust toolchain, which is the standard idiom for Rust packaging.

The `package()` function installs the compiled binary, a helper script (`printbar-watch`), a templated systemd user service (with `@BIN@` substituted to `/usr/bin`), an example configuration, and the LICENSE file — all into appropriate standard locations under `$pkgdir`. There are no suspicious operations: no `curl`/`wget` calls to unrelated hosts, no `base64`/encoded payloads, no `eval` of remote content, no `git pull` at build time, and no exfiltration or modification of files outside the package's own scope. The `printbar-watch` script and service unit originate from the upstream tarball and are not downloaded or executed from an external source at build time.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Standard Rust PKGBUILD with pinned source, checksum, and routine packaging steps.</summary>
</security_assessment>
